all_example_hypotheses.ambient_construction: Take M to be a smooth quadric threefold Q^3 in projective 4-space and L=O_Q(1).
all_example_hypotheses.anticanonical_check: By adjunction, K_Q=(K_P4+2H)|_Q=(-5H+2H)|_Q=-3L. Hence -K_Q=(d0+d1)L, with dim M=n+1=3 and L very ample.
all_example_hypotheses.genericity_check: Choose F0, F1 and F as generic sections of L, 2L and 3L. These are basepoint-free very ample systems, so generic divisors are smooth and all their intersections are transverse. The anticanonical pencil F0 F1+tF has a smooth general member; its finite exceptional parameter set can be avoided by shrinking the punctured disk. Adjunction gives trivial canonical bundle on its smooth fibers.
all_example_hypotheses.dimension_check: 1=m<=n-1=1; the deepest intersection E0 cap E1 is a smooth connected curve. Thus this is within the specified intermediate family, not an arbitrary formal degree choice outside its hypotheses.
all_example_hypotheses.scope: This is an analytic/algebraic realization argument using standard adjunction and genericity of very ample systems. No specific author coefficients or author code were needed or executed.

coordinate_check: For m=1 write a simplex point as (x,1-x). A quotient covector has effective coordinate q=p0-p1, invariant under adding c(1,1).
Then <(x,1-x)-(x',1-x'),p>=(x-x')q. At an interior differentiability point, the printed inequality for x'=x+h with both signs of h forces q=-U'(x). The standard subgradient instead has q=U'(x).
The target facets are p=(p0,0), -1/d0<=p0<=0, and p=(0,p1), -1/d1<=p1<=0. Thus the effective target is q in [-1/d0,1/d1]. The reflection error cannot be removed by the quotient convention.
decisive_evidence: Set n=2,d0=1,d1=2. Equation (18) gives U'(x)=-1+sqrt(3x/2) for 0<=x<=2/3, and U'(x)=(1-sqrt(3(1-x)))/2 for 2/3<=x<=1. Both branches are increasing and agree at zero at x=2/3; the total derivative range is [-1,1/2]. Integration therefore gives a convex function U.

This U also satisfies the required form (12) on Delta: for p in Delta^vee with q=p0-p1, define U_tilde(p)=p1+sup_{0<=s<=1}(q*s-U(s)). Since all classical subgradients of U lie in the target interval, sup_p(<(x,1-x),p>-U_tilde(p))=U(x). The function U_tilde is bounded on the compact target.

For E=(0,1/6), equation (18) has -1<U'(x)<-1/2, so the printed definition would require q=-U'(x) in (1/2,1). This lies outside the allowed target [-1,1/2], hence grad_print U(x) is empty at every x in E.
Consequently M_print U(E)=integral over the empty set of W dq=0.
The normalized source measure is mu0=dx on [0,1]. The paper's mass constant is C1=1/(n*d0)+1/(n*d1)=1/2+1/4=3/4. Therefore C1*mu0(E)=(3/4)*(1/6)=1/8.

The discrepancy 0 versus 1/8 is thus a genuine contradiction between the literal printed definition and its claimed application to Example 4.4. It is not a counterexample to the conventionally defined transport problem.

repair.correction: Replace <x-x',p> by <x'-x,p> in the displayed definition of Section 4.1.
verified_local_result: The corrected definition gives q=U'(x) at differentiability points and matches the standard supporting-plane convention in (12)-(13).
On E the corrected gradient image is (-1,-1/2), within the negative target facet, where W(q)=1+q. Its weighted mass is integral_{-1}^{-1/2}(1+q)dq=1/8, exactly the right-hand side.
On the whole first open branch, U''=3/(4*sqrt(3x/2)) and W(U')=sqrt(3x/2), giving W(U') U''=3/4.
On the second open branch, U''=3/(4*sqrt(3(1-x))) and W(U')=sqrt(3(1-x)), again giving 3/4. U' is continuous at the interior join, so no atomic mass is introduced there.

The general convex-duality identification and the standard Brenier gradient in the paper's next subsection have the corrected sign. This check validates the sign convention and the explicit example, not an independent reproof of all subsequent geometric theorems.
repair.repair_verification_scope: Complete local sign and explicit-example verification; global Calabi-Yau theorem not re-proved by this auxiliary check.

preserved_bounded_check.question: Does C-infinity approximation on a high-measure smooth compact set, with equal total mass, suffice for the regularized stability application?
preserved_bounded_check.result: Yes for the asymptotic application used in Corollary 6.4, under the regularization existence/local-approximation properties asserted in Remark 5.8. This check does not establish its stronger fixed-t arbitrary-TV approximation assertion.
assumptions: Fix t != 0 in the smooth family; write V=(L^n), mu=V mu_t, nu=omega_t^n. All are positive finite measures and nu(X_t)=mu(X_t)=V.

For any prescribed small eta>0, the good-region comparison in Proposition 5.6 allows t sufficiently small and a compact K in the smooth good region with mu(X_t\K)<=eta V and integral_K |nu-mu|<=eta V. Passing from an open good region to compact K costs an arbitrarily small mass, by inner regularity.

A smooth Kahler regularization omega_t,j is in the same cohomology class, tends locally smoothly to omega_t near K, and has arbitrarily small C0 potential difference, as asserted in Remark 5.8. The existence of this regularization is treated as a stated analytic dependency, not independently reproved here.
Local smooth convergence can be chosen after t and K are fixed, so integral_K |nu_j-nu|<=eta V where nu_j=omega_t,j^n. Its total mass is V by the common cohomology class.
complete_measure_estimate: Set a=integral_K |nu_j-mu|. The two local errors imply a<=2 eta V.
Equal total masses and positivity give nu_j(K^c)=V-nu_j(K)<=V-mu(K)+a=mu(K^c)+a.
Using the paper's integral absolute-difference convention for total variation, ||nu_j-mu||_TV <= a+nu_j(K^c)+mu(K^c) <= 2a+2mu(K^c) <= 6 eta V.

Thus for every prescribed stability tolerance gamma^(2n+3), first choose eta<gamma^(2n+3)/6, then t sufficiently small, then a sufficiently fine regularization for that t. No uniform smoothing scale or unjustified C0-to-TV continuity is required.
complete_stability_perturbation: Let lambda=|log|t|| and omega=omega_CY,t/lambda. If phi_t,j regularizes the ansatz potential phi_t, the smooth omega-psh function to use is q_j=-psi_t+(phi_t,j-phi_t)/lambda; then omega+dd^c q_j=omega_t,j/lambda.
From min psi_t=0, sup(-psi_t)=0. Choose ||q_j+psi_t||_C0<delta/8, so sup q_j>=-delta/8.
If the contrary hypothesis of Corollary 6.4 holds, mu_t({psi_t>delta})>delta. On that set q_j<-7delta/8, so the mass condition for Theorem 6.3 holds with a=-delta/2 and b=delta.
The uniform C0 bound is retained with one harmless fixed margin. The uniform Skoda estimate and its change of reference potential remain the paper's Theorems 6.1-6.2 dependencies.

Choose gamma below the theorem's allowed threshold and with C gamma<delta/8, then choose t and the regularization as above. Theorem 6.3 yields sup q_j<=-3delta/8, contradicting sup q_j>=-delta/8. The limiting weak estimate follows.
counterevidence_and_limits: C0 closeness of arbitrary potentials alone does not imply TV closeness of their Monge-Ampere measures; that inference is not used in the estimate above.

The proof above controls the regularized measure relative to V mu_t as t tends to zero. It does not by itself prove arbitrarily small TV distance to omega_t^n for every fixed t, which is stronger language in Remark 5.8.
No counterexample to that stronger fixed-t statement was constructed, and no Major finding is inferred from its not being independently established here.
The cited Skoda/capacity stability theorem and global regularization existence were not fetched or independently reproved; their stated hypotheses and the exact application were tracked.
preserved_bounded_check.assessment: Application justified by the displayed bounded argument with explicit analytic dependencies. No new substantive defect retained.

preserved_bounded_check.question: Does the X_t/U_{y,t} intermediate integration-domain inconsistency break the bound actually needed in Proposition 6.12?
preserved_bounded_check.source_observation: The image of PDF32 confirms that a global unweighted X_t integral is inserted after a weight bound established only on U_{y,t}. The displayed stronger intermediate inequality is not justified by that local estimate.
complete_local_replacement: Write lambda=|log|t||, Phi=phi_t+lambda psi_t, and dV=i^(n^2)Omega_t wedge conjugate(Omega_t), a positive measure.
The preceding local estimates give Phi<=lambda u(y)+C lambda epsilon on U=U_{y,t}. For I=int_Xt |s|_h^(2l) exp(-2l Phi) dV, positivity gives I>=int_U |s|_h^(2l) exp(-2l Phi) dV.

Apply the local weight bound only on U: I>=exp[-2l lambda u(y)-C l lambda epsilon] int_U |s|_h^(2l) dV. This is exactly the final lower bound used by the proof, with an adjusted constant. The unnecessary stronger global unweighted line can be deleted.
Taking log and dividing by 2l gives (1/l)log||s||_{y,t} <= (1/(2l))log I+lambda u(y)+C lambda epsilon, using the annular norm convention in the paper's subsequent displayed step.

The existing Ohsawa-Takegoshi estimate supplies (1/(2l))log I<=-Phi(z)+C lambda/l. Combining it with Corollary 6.11 gives a bound for every decomposition coefficient. No global estimate of Phi on all X_t is needed.

The point normalization |s(z)|=1 and the finite-decomposition triangle inequality select a coefficient tuple alpha using only z and s, so the same tuple works for every admissible y. This preserves the quantifier required for the later Legendre optimization.

Rearrangement yields psi_t(z)<=-phi_t(z)/lambda+u(y)+sum_i alpha_i log|F_i(z)|/(l lambda)+sum_i alpha_i y_i/l+C/l+C epsilon+C(l)/lambda. For fixed epsilon and l choose t small enough to absorb C(l)/lambda into a constant multiple of 1/l, exactly as stated on PDF33.

reasons: The source images on PDF16-18 distinguish the literal reflected subgradient from the conventional Brenier map on PDF17. Recomputing n=2,d0=1,d1=2 gives the admissible target [-1,1/2], empty printed gradient on E=(0,1/6), and 0 versus 1/8 mass; correcting the supporting-plane sign restores 1/8. The surrounding proof consistently uses the corrected convention, so the documented sign slip does not establish failure of its intended central inference.

The positivity/equal-mass estimate a<=2 eta V implies total variation <=2a+2mu(Kc)<=6 eta V. The perturbation q_j=-psi_t+(phi_t,j-phi_t)/lambda, with eta then t then j chosen, supplies the stated sufficient stability application. The report correctly retains local-smooth regularization and Skoda/stability as dependencies and does not claim the stronger fixed-t TV assertion proved or false.

PDF32-33 confirm the unnecessary stronger global unweighted intermediate integral and the terminal local annulus bound. Restricting the positive weighted integral to U before bounding its weight establishes exactly the used terminal inequality; the coefficient is selected from z,s independently of y. The existing limited correction does not establish a false main theorem.
